headline: Haplotype-resolved assembly of heterozygous genomes from long reads
label: Haplotype Resolved Genome Assembly
summary: Recent work targets switch errors, reference bias, and reference-guided reassembly in long-read haplotype-resolved genome assembly.
synthesis: The dominant thread is haplotype resolution treated as an explicit analytical objective, with heterozygous diploid or highly heterozygous genomes reconstructed as separate haplotype sequences rather than collapsed onto one reference. PhaseGrass produces chromosome-level haplotype-resolved assemblies of highly heterozygous grass genomes, applied to Lolium, avoiding reference bias without parental data. snpphaser targets the phasing stage itself, phasing high-quality heterozygous variants first and then filtering inconsistent low-quality variants to reduce switch errors in long-read data. RefLA takes the complementary route of reference-assisted assembly from long reads, pairing alignment-guided structural refinement with localized reassembly. What is new across these items is that phasing accuracy and reference handling are treated as distinct, separately engineered steps in building haplotype-resolved assemblies directly from reads.
